standard.title: Create critical written and multimodal texts
standard.description: plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, organising, expanding and developing ideas, and selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standard.prior_knowledge: Students plan, create and publish texts selecting structures, language features and literary devices for purpose (AC9E7LY06). They have not yet developed analytical and critical text types, or focused on multi-element selection across structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features simultaneously.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for purposes and audiences across imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and critical modes.

nodes.label: Planning and structuring for analytical/critical purposes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a written text with an argument structure: contention, sequenced supporting points and conclusion.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan and draft a text with a clear contention, at least two sequenced supporting points and a conclusion — demonstrating that the structure serves the argument.
nodes.typical_width: Plan and develop an argument with a contention followed by a series of linked and sequenced paragraphs that develop a line of argument, ending with a conclusion that summarises the main argument.
wider: Plan a complex argument that includes acknowledgement and refutation of a counter-position, evaluating how this strengthens the argument structure
Compare effective planning strategies across text types — argument, analysis, explanation — identifying what changes and what stays the same

response_modes.reason: Argument structure is a reasoning scaffold as much as a text structure. Students who understand what a contention, supporting point and conclusion do — not just what they are — can plan arguments that actually argue. The logical architecture needs explicit modelling.

success_criteria: Student's plan includes a clear contention and at least two supporting points that develop a line of argument
Student can explain how the planned structure serves the argument's purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot produce a planned argument structure with contention and linked supporting points cannot attempt N2 text creation — the creation task presupposes an understood structural scaffold to populate with language and device choices.

nodes.label: Creating with selected language and device choices
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts selecting appropriate text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for their specific purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text that makes deliberate selections of at least one structural and one language/device choice, and can explain why each choice suits the purpose and audience.
nodes.typical_width: Create informative or analytical texts with well-chosen facts and precise language; or imaginative/persuasive texts with deliberate literary and structural device selections; discussing literary device choices and evaluating their potential effects on an audience.
wider: Create a text that deliberately subverts a conventional structure for this text type, and evaluate the effect of the subversion on purpose and audience
Create a multimodal text and evaluate how the multimodal choices expand or complicate what could be achieved in written mode alone

response_modes.reason: The descriptor names four simultaneous selection dimensions: text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features. Coordinating deliberate selections across all four — rather than making one choice at a time — is the compositional integration this node targets.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Text creation with deliberate device selection is intrinsically motivating for Y9 and directly develops transferable writing capability. Discussing choices with a peer and evaluating effects (as the elaboration specifies) is pedagogically rich — it makes tacit compositional knowledge explicit.
success_criteria: Student makes at least two deliberate selection decisions (structure, language, device or multimodal) and can explain why
Student's text demonstrates — not just states — the intended purpose and audience awareness

nodes.label: Editing and publishing for accuracy and effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit written and multimodal texts for grammatical accuracy, spelling and punctuation, and to improve clarity and organisation for specific purposes and audiences.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a draft text addressing at least one accuracy issue (grammar, spelling or punctuation) and one effectiveness issue (clarity, organisation, or device choice), explaining the reasoning for each revision.
nodes.typical_width: Review and edit texts for accuracy of grammar, spelling and punctuation, and to achieve particular purposes and address specific audiences — improving clarity and control through organising, developing, extending and linking ideas.
wider: Develop a personal editing checklist calibrated to your own known error patterns, and apply it to produce a publishable draft
Peer-edit a classmate's text and provide targeted feedback on both accuracy and effectiveness — distinguishing between non-negotiable errors and matters of style

response_modes.reason: Editing requires mechanical fluency — the ability to attend to accuracy while also holding the text's purpose in view. Students improve through repeated editing practice across different text types, not through additional conceptual instruction.

success_criteria: Student corrects at least one accuracy error and makes at least one effectiveness revision
Student can explain the reasoning for at least one revision decision
